questions: What does it mean for a string S to be "good" in terms of the operations involving A, R, C characters when the initial sequence A consists only of 0s and 1s?
Are the characters A, R, C in the operations referring to specific fixed characters or are they placeholders for values from the sequence A?
Is the sequence A provided in the input related to the string S we are trying to construct, and if so, how?
What is the exact condition that makes a string S satisfy the "good string" property - is it based on being able to perform operations until some terminal state?
In the operation descriptions, what happens to the string S after performing the operations - do we modify S or only the sequence A?
Does "perform the following operation any number of times" mean we can apply these operations iteratively on the same data structure, and what constitutes a valid final state?
Are we determining if there exists any binary string S of length N such that the given operations can be applied, or is S derived from the input sequence A in some way?
What is the relationship between the indices wrapping around (using S_{N+1}=S_1, etc.) and the actual operations - do the operations wrap around the string indices as well?
answers: S is good if the given operations can be applied until sequence A contains no 0, using characters matching the A/R/C pattern requirements.
A, R, C are fixed characters that S's characters must match at specific positions; they aren't derived from A's values.
A is the fixed input sequence being transformed; S is a separate string being sought, not derived from A.
S is good if the operations can be performed any number of times so that A ends up containing no 0.
Only sequence A is modified by the operations; S remains fixed throughout.
Operations may be applied repeatedly to the current state of A; a valid final state is any state where A contains no 0.
We are determining whether there exists some string S of length N (over the required alphabet) for which the operations can transform A to contain no 0; S is not derived from A.
Only as given by the stated wraparound definitions; not specified further.
inline_prompts: You are given a positive integer N and a sequence A=(A_1,A_2,\dots,A_N) of length N, consisting of 0 and 1. We call a string S of length N, a good string if the given operations can be applied until sequence A contains no 0, using characters matching the A/R/C pattern requirements. We call a string S of length N, a good string if it is possible to perform the following operation any number of times (possibly zero). Here, S_i (1\leq i\leq N) denotes the i-th character of S, and we define S_{N+1}=S_1, S_{N+2}=S_2, and A_{N+1}=A_1. - Perform one of the following operations: - Choose an integer i with 1\leq i\leq N such that S_i= A, S_{i+1}= R, and S_{i+2}= C, and replace each of A_i and A_{i+1} with 1. - Choose an integer i with 1\leq i\leq N such that S_{i+2}= A, S_{i+1}= R, and S_i= C, and replace each of A_i and A_{i+1} with 1. Determine whether there exists a good string. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N A_1 A_2 \dots A_N Output If there exists a good string, print Yes; otherwise, print No. The judge is case-insensitive; for example, if the correct answer is Yes, outputs such as yes, YES, or yEs will also be accepted. Constraints - 3\leq N\leq 200000 - A_i\in \lbrace 0,1 \rbrace (1\leq i\leq N) - All input values are integers.
